Tofu, also known as bean curd, is a food made by coagulating and pressing soy milk into soft white blocks. It originated in China over two thousand years ago, with its invention often attributed to Prince Liu An of the Han Dynasty, and later spread to Japan and other parts of East and Southeast Asia. Tofu is a staple protein source in many Asian cuisines and, in the West, is frequently used as a meat substitute due to its nutritional profile. The English name derives from the Japanese "tōfu," which itself borrowed the term from Chinese. It is valued not only for its culinary versatility but also for its relatively low environmental impact in terms of land use and greenhouse gas emissions per gram of protein produced.
